rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese word for the flying mammal.

example.english: I saw a bat flying near my home last night.
example.traditional: 我噚晚見到一隻蝙蝠喺屋企附近飛。
example.jyutping: ngo5 cam4 maan5 gin3 dou2 jat1 zek3 pin1 fuk1 hai2 uk1 kei2 fu6 gan6 fei1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for hitting an object with a bat or as if with one.

example.english: I use a bat to hit the ball.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jung6 zi1 kau4 paang5 daa2 go3 bo1

rows.note: Use this for the bat used to hit a ball in sports, especially baseball or softball.

example.english: The bat slipped out of my hands while I was playing baseball.
example.traditional: 我打棒球嗰陣，球棒從手上滑咗落嚟。
example.jyutping: ngo5 daa2 paang5 kau4 go2 zan6 kau4 paang5 cung4 sau2 soeng6 waat6 zo2 lok6 lei4

rows.note: Use this for a light strike or swipe at something, such as a cat batting at a toy.

example.english: I saw the cat bat at a little ball.
example.traditional: 我見到隻貓拍個波波玩。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gin3 dou2 zek3 maau1 paak3 go3 bo1 bo1 waan2

rows.note: Use this sports-context construction to say that A's turn has come to bat rather than field.
Use this when the bat is being treated as a stick or club used as a weapon.

example.english: Someone chased me with a bat, so I ran away.
example.traditional: 有人拎住支棍追住我，我即刻走。
example.jyutping: jau5 jan4 ling1 zyu6 zi1 gwan3 zeoi1 zyu6 ngo5 ngo5 zik1 hak1 zau2

rows.note: Use this for blinking or fluttering the eyelashes, especially in the phrase 眨眼.

example.english: I saw her bat her eyes at me.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gin3 dou2 keoi5 hoeng3 ngo5 zaam2 ngaan5

rows.note: Use this mainly in baseball terminology for a player's turn at bat.

example.english: I had three turns at bat in this game.
example.traditional: 我今場比賽有三個打席。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 coeng4 bei2 coi3 jau5 saam1 go3 daa2 zik6
